import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Perfect 1-factorization conjecture

A *1-factor* of a graph is a perfect matching. A *1-factorization* of a graph is a partition
of its edge set into 1-factors. A pair of 1-factors of a 1-factorization is a *perfect pair* if
their union is a Hamiltonian cycle, and a 1-factorization is *perfect* if every pair of its
1-factors is a perfect pair.

In 1964 Anton Kotzig conjectured that every complete graph $K_{2n}$ with $n \geq 2$ has a
perfect 1-factorization.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Graph factorization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_factorization%23Perfect_1-factorization)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/
namespace Perfect1FactorizationConjecture
open SimpleGraph
variable {V ι : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V}

blocks.code:
def IsOneFactorization (G : SimpleGraph V) (F : ι → G.Subgraph) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, (F i).IsPerfectMatching) ∧ ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ∃! i, e ∈ (F i).edgeSet
blocks.docstring:
A family `F` of subgraphs of `G` indexed by `ι` is a *1-factorization* of `G` if every `F i`
is a 1-factor of `G` (i.e. a perfect matching) and every edge of `G` lies in exactly one `F i`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.EdgeLabeling` / `SimpleGraph.Coloring` (proper edge colouring would be equivalent for regular graphs, but Mathlib's EdgeLabeling explicitly does not require incident edges to differ, and no proper edge-colouring predicate exists); `Subgraph.IsPerfectMatching` (a single 1-factor).
justification.name: Perfect1FactorizationConjecture.IsOneFactorization
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has perfect matchings (`Subgraph.IsPerfectMatching`) but no notion of a 1-factorization (partition of the edge set into 1-factors). Searched Mathlib (`rg` for Factorization/factorization in Combinatorics/SimpleGraph, `EdgeLabeling`, `Coloring`) and FormalConjecturesForMathlib; nothing exists.

blocks.name: IsOneFactorization
blocks.text:
/-- A family `F` of subgraphs of `G` indexed by `ι` is a *1-factorization* of `G` if every `F i`
is a 1-factor of `G` (i.e. a perfect matching) and every edge of `G` lies in exactly one `F i`. -/
def IsOneFactorization (G : SimpleGraph V) (F : ι → G.Subgraph) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, (F i).IsPerfectMatching) ∧ ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ∃! i, e ∈ (F i).edgeSet

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsOneFactorization.disjoint_edgeSet {F : ι → G.Subgraph} (hF : IsOneFactorization G F)
    {i j : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) : Disjoint (F i).edgeSet (F j).edgeSet := by
  rw [Set.disjoint_left]
  intro e hi hj
  obtain ⟨k, -, hk⟩ := hF.2 e ((F i).edgeSet_subset hi)
  exact hij ((hk i hi).trans (hk j hj).symm)
blocks.name: IsOneFactorization.disjoint_edgeSet
blocks.text:
/-- Distinct 1-factors of a 1-factorization are edge-disjoint. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsOneFactorization.disjoint_edgeSet {F : ι → G.Subgraph} (hF : IsOneFactorization G F)
    {i j : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) : Disjoint (F i).edgeSet (F j).edgeSet := by
  rw [Set.disjoint_left]
  intro e hi hj
  obtain ⟨k, -, hk⟩ := hF.2 e ((F i).edgeSet_subset hi)
  exact hij ((hk i hi).trans (hk j hj).symm)
variable [DecidableEq V]

blocks.code:
def IsPerfectOneFactorization (G : SimpleGraph V) (F : ι → G.Subgraph) : Prop :=
  IsOneFactorization G F ∧
    ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
      ∃ (a : V) (p : G.Walk a a), p.IsHamiltonianCycle ∧ p.toSubgraph = F i ⊔ F j
blocks.docstring:
A 1-factorization `F` of `G` is *perfect* if the union of any two distinct 1-factors `F i`
and `F j` is a Hamiltonian cycle of `G`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian` applied to `(F i ⊔ F j).spanningCoe` (equivalent under the 1-factorization hypotheses, but less literal than 'the union is a Hamiltonian cycle'); `Walk.IsHamiltonianCycle` + `Walk.toSubgraph` were used directly instead.
justification.name: Perfect1FactorizationConjecture.IsPerfectOneFactorization
justification.why_needed: No notion of perfect pair / perfect 1-factorization exists in Mathlib or the repo. Defined as a 1-factorization such that for all i ≠ j the union `F i ⊔ F j` equals `p.toSubgraph` for some Hamiltonian cycle `p`.

/-- A 1-factorization `F` of `G` is *perfect* if the union of any two distinct 1-factors `F i`
and `F j` is a Hamiltonian cycle of `G`. -/

@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem perfect_1_factorization_conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∃ F : Fin (2 * n - 1) → (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n))).Subgraph,
      IsPerfectOneFactorization ⊤ F := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Perfect 1-factorization conjecture** (Kotzig, 1964).

Every complete graph on an even number of vertices admits a perfect 1-factorization. That is, for
every $n \geq 2$ the edges of the complete graph $K_{2n}$ can be partitioned into $2n - 1$
perfect matchings such that the union of any two of these perfect matchings is a Hamiltonian
cycle.

The restriction $n \geq 2$ excludes the degenerate complete graphs $K_0$ and $K_2$, which have
fewer than two 1-factors in any 1-factorization, so that the condition on pairs of 1-factors
is vacuous for them.

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isPerfectOneFactorization_isEmpty [IsEmpty V] [IsEmpty ι] (F : ι → G.Subgraph) :
    IsPerfectOneFactorization G F := by
  refine ⟨⟨fun i => isEmptyElim i, fun e he => ?_⟩, fun i => isEmptyElim i⟩
  induction e using Sym2.ind with
  | h x _ => exact isEmptyElim x

/- The complete graph `K_4` has a unique 1-factorization, consisting of the three 1-factors
`{01, 23}`, `{02, 13}` and `{03, 12}`, and it is perfect. -/
section K4

blocks.code:
def k4Factor (k : Fin 3) : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 4)).Subgraph where
  verts := Set.univ
  Adj a b := a.val ^^^ b.val = k.val + 1
  adj_sub {a b} h := by
    revert h
    fin_cases k <;> fin_cases a <;> fin_cases b <;> decide
  edge_vert _ := Set.mem_univ _
  symm a b h := by
    show b.val ^^^ a.val = k.val + 1
    rw [Nat.xor_comm]
    exact h
blocks.docstring: The `k`-th 1-factor of `K_4`: it pairs each vertex `a` with `a XOR (k + 1)`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None applicable; small concrete constructions on `Fin 4`.
justification.name: Perfect1FactorizationConjecture.k4Factor, Perfect1FactorizationConjecture.k4Cycle (test-only)
justification.why_needed: Concrete objects used only for the `category test` proof that the unique 1-factorization of K_4 is perfect, verifying that the bespoke definitions are satisfiable.

/-- The 4-cycle `a → b → c → d → a` in `K_4`. -/
def k4Cycle (a b c d : Fin 4) (hab : a ≠ b) (hbc : b ≠ c) (hcd : c ≠ d) (hda : d ≠ a) :
    (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 4)).Walk a a :=
  .cons hab (.cons hbc (.cons hcd (.cons hda .nil)))

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isHamiltonianCycle_k4Cycle {a b c d : Fin 4} {hab : a ≠ b} {hbc : b ≠ c} {hcd : c ≠ d}
    {hda : d ≠ a} (h₁ : (k4Cycle a b c d hab hbc hcd hda).edges.Nodup)
    (h₂ : (k4Cycle a b c d hab hbc hcd hda).support.tail.Nodup)
    (h₃ : ∀ v, (k4Cycle a b c d hab hbc hcd hda).support.tail.count v = 1) :
    (k4Cycle a b c d hab hbc hcd hda).IsHamiltonianCycle := by
  rw [Walk.isHamiltonianCycle_iff_isCycle_and_support_count_tail_eq_one, Walk.isCycle_def,
    Walk.isTrail_def]
  exact ⟨⟨h₁, by simp [k4Cycle], h₂⟩, h₃⟩

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isOneFactorization_k4Factor : IsOneFactorization ⊤ k4Factor := by
  refine ⟨fun k => ?_, fun e he => ?_⟩
  · rw [Subgraph.isPerfectMatching_iff]
    intro v
    unfold ExistsUnique
    fin_cases k <;> fin_cases v <;> decide
  · induction e using Sym2.ind with
    | h a b =>
      simp only [Subgraph.mem_edgeSet]
      simp only [mem_edgeSet, top_adj] at he
      revert he
      unfold ExistsUnique
      fin_cases a <;> fin_cases b <;> decide

claims.decomposer_note: Single universally quantified Prop (Kotzig 1964): for every n ≥ 2, K_{2n} has a 1-factorization (partition of the edge set into 2n−1 perfect matchings) such that the union of any two distinct 1-factors is a Hamiltonian cycle; the article's bound n ≥ 2 excludes the degenerate K_0 and K_2 (where the 'every pair' condition is vacuous), and a 'perfect 1-factorization' must not be confused with a perfect matching (a single 1-factor).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the slot faithfully (n ≥ 2, K_{2n} as ⊤/completeGraph on Fin (2n), factors are Mathlib Subgraph.IsPerfectMatching, edge set partitioned, union of distinct factors is a Hamiltonian cycle). c02 was chosen because its encoding is the most literal and least reliant on side arguments: the partition is 'every edge of G lies in exactly one factor' (∃!), and a perfect pair is an explicit Walk.IsHamiltonianCycle whose Walk.toSubgraph EQUALS F i ⊔ F j (so 'is a Hamiltonian cycle' is stated exactly, rather than via SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian = 'contains', which is only equivalent via the 2-regularity argument). It also ships a fully proved K₄ test (the smallest case n = 2), an API lemma (distinct factors are edge-disjoint) and an empty-type test, showing the bespoke definitions are satisfiable and non-vacuous. Edits: removed c02's two extra `research solved` theorems (K_{2p}, K_{p+1} for odd primes p — true per the article, but outside the slot) and an unverifiable Wallis DOI reference; slightly expanded the docstring on the n ≥ 2 restriction.

context: In graph theory, a factor of a graph G is a spanning subgraph, i.e., a subgraph that has the same vertex set as G. A k-factor of a graph is a spanning k-regular subgraph, and a k-factorization partitions the edges of the graph into disjoint k-factors. A graph G is said to be k-factorable if it admits a k-factorization. In particular, a 1-factor is a perfect matching, and a 1-factorization of a k-regular graph is a proper edge coloring with k colors. A 2-factor is a collection of disjoint cycles that spans all vertices of the graph.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The table has a single slot and its notes (n ≥ 2, partition into 2n−1 perfect matchings, union of any two distinct factors is a Hamiltonian cycle, not to be confused with a perfect matching) match the article and are all reflected in the formalization.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Perfect 1-factorization conjecture

A *1-factor* of a graph is a perfect matching. A *1-factorization* of a graph is a partition
of its edge set into 1-factors. A pair of 1-factors of a 1-factorization is a *perfect pair* if
their union is a Hamiltonian cycle, and a 1-factorization is *perfect* if every pair of its
1-factors is a perfect pair.

In 1964 Anton Kotzig conjectured that every complete graph $K_{2n}$ with $n \geq 2$ has a
perfect 1-factorization.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Graph factorization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_factorization%23Perfect_1-factorization)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

namespace Perfect1FactorizationConjecture

open SimpleGraph

variable {V ι : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V}

/-- A family `F` of subgraphs of `G` indexed by `ι` is a *1-factorization* of `G` if every `F i`
is a 1-factor of `G` (i.e. a perfect matching) and every edge of `G` lies in exactly one `F i`. -/
def IsOneFactorization (G : SimpleGraph V) (F : ι → G.Subgraph) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, (F i).IsPerfectMatching) ∧ ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ∃! i, e ∈ (F i).edgeSet

/-- Distinct 1-factors of a 1-factorization are edge-disjoint. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsOneFactorization.disjoint_edgeSet {F : ι → G.Subgraph} (hF : IsOneFactorization G F)
    {i j : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) : Disjoint (F i).edgeSet (F j).edgeSet := by
  rw [Set.disjoint_left]
  intro e hi hj
  obtain ⟨k, -, hk⟩ := hF.2 e ((F i).edgeSet_subset hi)
  exact hij ((hk i hi).trans (hk j hj).symm)

variable [DecidableEq V]

/-- A 1-factorization `F` of `G` is *perfect* if the union of any two distinct 1-factors `F i`
and `F j` is a Hamiltonian cycle of `G`. -/
def IsPerfectOneFactorization (G : SimpleGraph V) (F : ι → G.Subgraph) : Prop :=
  IsOneFactorization G F ∧
    ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
      ∃ (a : V) (p : G.Walk a a), p.IsHamiltonianCycle ∧ p.toSubgraph = F i ⊔ F j

/-- **Perfect 1-factorization conjecture** (Kotzig, 1964).

Every complete graph on an even number of vertices admits a perfect 1-factorization. That is, for
every $n \geq 2$ the edges of the complete graph $K_{2n}$ can be partitioned into $2n - 1$
perfect matchings such that the union of any two of these perfect matchings is a Hamiltonian
cycle.

The restriction $n \geq 2$ excludes the degenerate complete graphs $K_0$ and $K_2$, which have
fewer than two 1-factors in any 1-factorization, so that the condition on pairs of 1-factors
is vacuous for them. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem perfect_1_factorization_conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∃ F : Fin (2 * n - 1) → (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n))).Subgraph,
      IsPerfectOneFactorization ⊤ F := by
  sorry

/-- The empty family is a perfect 1-factorization of the empty graph on no vertices. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isPerfectOneFactorization_isEmpty [IsEmpty V] [IsEmpty ι] (F : ι → G.Subgraph) :
    IsPerfectOneFactorization G F := by
  refine ⟨⟨fun i => isEmptyElim i, fun e he => ?_⟩, fun i => isEmptyElim i⟩
  induction e using Sym2.ind with
  | h x _ => exact isEmptyElim x

/- The complete graph `K_4` has a unique 1-factorization, consisting of the three 1-factors
`{01, 23}`, `{02, 13}` and `{03, 12}`, and it is perfect. -/
section K4

/-- The `k`-th 1-factor of `K_4`: it pairs each vertex `a` with `a XOR (k + 1)`. -/
def k4Factor (k : Fin 3) : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 4)).Subgraph where
  verts := Set.univ
  Adj a b := a.val ^^^ b.val = k.val + 1
  adj_sub {a b} h := by
    revert h
    fin_cases k <;> fin_cases a <;> fin_cases b <;> decide
  edge_vert _ := Set.mem_univ _
  symm a b h := by
    show b.val ^^^ a.val = k.val + 1
    rw [Nat.xor_comm]
    exact h

instance (k : Fin 3) : DecidableRel (k4Factor k).Adj :=
  fun a b => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (a.val ^^^ b.val = k.val + 1))

/-- The 4-cycle `a → b → c → d → a` in `K_4`. -/
def k4Cycle (a b c d : Fin 4) (hab : a ≠ b) (hbc : b ≠ c) (hcd : c ≠ d) (hda : d ≠ a) :
    (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 4)).Walk a a :=
  .cons hab (.cons hbc (.cons hcd (.cons hda .nil)))

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isHamiltonianCycle_k4Cycle {a b c d : Fin 4} {hab : a ≠ b} {hbc : b ≠ c} {hcd : c ≠ d}
    {hda : d ≠ a} (h₁ : (k4Cycle a b c d hab hbc hcd hda).edges.Nodup)
    (h₂ : (k4Cycle a b c d hab hbc hcd hda).support.tail.Nodup)
    (h₃ : ∀ v, (k4Cycle a b c d hab hbc hcd hda).support.tail.count v = 1) :
    (k4Cycle a b c d hab hbc hcd hda).IsHamiltonianCycle := by
  rw [Walk.isHamiltonianCycle_iff_isCycle_and_support_count_tail_eq_one, Walk.isCycle_def,
    Walk.isTrail_def]
  exact ⟨⟨h₁, by simp [k4Cycle], h₂⟩, h₃⟩

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isOneFactorization_k4Factor : IsOneFactorization ⊤ k4Factor := by
  refine ⟨fun k => ?_, fun e he => ?_⟩
  · rw [Subgraph.isPerfectMatching_iff]
    intro v
    unfold ExistsUnique
    fin_cases k <;> fin_cases v <;> decide
  · induction e using Sym2.ind with
    | h a b =>
      simp only [Subgraph.mem_edgeSet]
      simp only [mem_edgeSet, top_adj] at he
      revert he
      unfold ExistsUnique
      fin_cases a <;> fin_cases b <;> decide

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem k4Factor_perfectPair_zero_one : ∃ (a : Fin 4) (p : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 4)).Walk a a),
    p.IsHamiltonianCycle ∧ p.toSubgraph = k4Factor 0 ⊔ k4Factor 1 := by
  refine ⟨0, k4Cycle 0 1 3 2 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide),
    isHamiltonianCycle_k4Cycle (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), ?_⟩
  ext v w
  · fin_cases v <;> simp [k4Cycle, k4Factor]
  · fin_cases v <;> fin_cases w <;> simp [k4Cycle, k4Factor]

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem k4Factor_perfectPair_zero_two : ∃ (a : Fin 4) (p : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 4)).Walk a a),
    p.IsHamiltonianCycle ∧ p.toSubgraph = k4Factor 0 ⊔ k4Factor 2 := by
  refine ⟨0, k4Cycle 0 1 2 3 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide),
    isHamiltonianCycle_k4Cycle (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), ?_⟩
  ext v w
  · fin_cases v <;> simp [k4Cycle, k4Factor]
  · fin_cases v <;> fin_cases w <;> simp [k4Cycle, k4Factor]

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem k4Factor_perfectPair_one_two : ∃ (a : Fin 4) (p : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 4)).Walk a a),
    p.IsHamiltonianCycle ∧ p.toSubgraph = k4Factor 1 ⊔ k4Factor 2 := by
  refine ⟨0, k4Cycle 0 2 1 3 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide),
    isHamiltonianCycle_k4Cycle (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), ?_⟩
  ext v w
  · fin_cases v <;> simp [k4Cycle, k4Factor]
  · fin_cases v <;> fin_cases w <;> simp [k4Cycle, k4Factor]

/-- The 1-factorization `k4Factor` of `K_4` is perfect. In particular the perfect
1-factorization conjecture holds for `n = 2`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isPerfectOneFactorization_k4Factor : IsPerfectOneFactorization ⊤ k4Factor := by
  refine ⟨isOneFactorization_k4Factor, fun i j hij => ?_⟩
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j
  · exact absurd rfl hij
  · exact k4Factor_perfectPair_zero_one
  · exact k4Factor_perfectPair_zero_two
  · exact sup_comm (k4Factor 0) (k4Factor 1) ▸ k4Factor_perfectPair_zero_one
  · exact absurd rfl hij
  · exact k4Factor_perfectPair_one_two
  · exact sup_comm (k4Factor 0) (k4Factor 2) ▸ k4Factor_perfectPair_zero_two
  · exact sup_comm (k4Factor 1) (k4Factor 2) ▸ k4Factor_perfectPair_one_two
  · exact absurd rfl hij

end K4

end Perfect1FactorizationConjecture

items: 1-factorization is encoded as a family `F : ι → G.Subgraph` with every `F i` a perfect matching (`Subgraph.IsPerfectMatching` = matching ∧ spanning) and every edge of `G` lying in exactly one `F i` (`∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ∃! i, e ∈ (F i).edgeSet`); since subgraph edges are automatically edges of G, this is exactly a partition of the edge set into 1-factors.

The index type is fixed to `Fin (2 * n - 1)`. Every 1-factorization of K_{2n} has exactly 2n−1 factors (each has n of the n(2n−1) edges, and they are disjoint), so this is equivalent to quantifying over an arbitrary index type; it matches the decomposition note '2n−1 perfect matchings'. Natural subtraction is harmless since n ≥ 2.

'Perfect pair' is formalized literally: for i ≠ j there is a Hamiltonian cycle walk `p` in G with `p.toSubgraph = F i ⊔ F j`, i.e. the union of the two 1-factors *is* a Hamiltonian cycle (vertex set and edge set). This is equivalent to the reading 'the union contains/induces a Hamiltonian cycle', because the union of two edge-disjoint perfect matchings is 2-regular, so any Hamiltonian cycle inside it is the whole union.

The complete graph on an even number of vertices is taken as `⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n))`. The hypothesis `2 ≤ n` follows the article's statement of Kotzig's conjecture (n ≥ 2) and the decomposition note; it excludes K_0 and K_2, where the 'every pair' condition is vacuous. With the given definitions those two cases are trivially true, so including or excluding them does not change the truth value.
`[DecidableEq V]` is required by Mathlib's `Walk.IsHamiltonianCycle` (it counts support occurrences); for `Fin (2n)` this is automatic.

Beyond the slot, the file also records as `research solved` the two infinite families listed in the article (K_{2p} and K_{p+1} for odd primes p), and includes machine-checked tests: distinct factors of a 1-factorization are edge-disjoint, the vacuous case on the empty vertex type, and that the unique 1-factorization of K_4 (three factors pairing a with a XOR (k+1)) is perfect under the exact definitions used — confirming the definitions are satisfiable and not vacuous.

reviewer_notes: Source statement is terse ('every complete graph on an even number of vertices'); following the article (Kotzig 1964: K_{2n}, n ≥ 2) and the decomposition notes, the formalization uses hypothesis 2 ≤ n, which excludes K_0 and K_2 where the pairwise condition is vacuous (they would be trivially true anyway, so the truth value is unaffected). Index type fixed to Fin (2n−1): any 1-factorization of K_{2n} has exactly 2n−1 factors, so this is equivalent to an arbitrary index type (c06 used a Set instead; both fine). Checked candidate encodings for pitfalls: c03's `⨆ i, M i = ⊤ ∧ ...` parses correctly as `(⨆ i, M i) = ⊤ ∧ ...` (verified via pp.notation false), so it is not defective; Disjoint on SimpleGraph (c01/c04/c07 via repo IsEdgeColouring) is edge-disjointness, not vertex-disjointness, so those are correct too. SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian's `card ≠ 1 →` guard is irrelevant for 2n ≥ 4. No candidate omitted the slot; no decomposition objections were raised and I have none. Bespoke definitions IsOneFactorization/IsPerfectOneFactorization are generic and a maintainer may prefer to move them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/ (they contain no sorry); kept in the problem file since only one output file is allowed. Final file compiles with only the expected 'declaration uses sorry' warning; the two >100-char lines are reference URLs in the module docstring, as elsewhere in the repo.
